- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use lagged mean.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast gradually, not abruptly.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or flat; model tends to hold trend; apply smoothing or decay factor to recent highs/lows.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend + negative sentiment, model often ignores it; add 1–2% downward bias unless sentiment reverses.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
